newsitem.title: USA: IMF steps up oversight of world hot spots-IMF head.
newsitem.headline: IMF steps up oversight of world hot spots-IMF head.

text.p: International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus said Thursday the IMF has stepped up its surveillance of what he called the world economy's "hot spots" but declined to say where they were.

Speaking to reporters ahead of the start of the semi-annual meeting of the IMF and World Bank, Camdessus though played down speculation that Japan, South Korea or Brazil might be designated in that way.
He did though say that the IMF was pressing Thailand to take further measures to put its economy into better balance.
Camdessus saw no reason to be alarmed about the outlook for the Japanese, South Korean or Brazilian economies.
He said that Tokyo was making "strong efforts" to put its financial sector in order and to ensure that its incipient recovery continues. "We don't see any reasons for alarm there," Camdessus said.

He added that he viewed "with satisfaction" the way that South Korea has handled its economic difficulties. "We are confident that they will continue, keep the economy growing and reducing their current account deficit," Camdessus said.
"I wouldn't say that everything is perfect in Brazil," Camdessus said. But he added, "Here also I would be very surprised if we were to have a major shock in the next few months."
As for Thailand, he said the country has taken a "few significant steps" to buttress its financial sector and to slow demand in order to reduce its current account deficit.
"We are pressing them to take additional steps," the IMF chief said. "They are considering that. We are hopeful that they will continue acting this way," he added.
